import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class B {
    static BufferedReader r = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
    static PrintWriter pw = new PrintWriter(System.out);
    
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        StringTokenizer st = new StringTokenizer(r.readLine());
        int n = Integer.parseInt(st.nextToken());
        double p = Double.parseDouble(st.nextToken());
        
        int ans = 0;
        
        // Try each possible number of maps to study (from 0 to n)
        for (int studied = 0; studied <= n; studied++) {
            double prob = calculateProbability(n, studied);
            if (prob >= p) {
                ans = studied;
                break;
            }
        }
        
        pw.print(ans);
        pw.close();
    }
    
    // Calculate probability that the game is played on a studied map
    // when 'studied' maps are studied out of 'n' total maps
    public static double calculateProbability(int n, int studied) {
        if (studied == 0) {
            return 0.0;
        }
        
        // Total ways to choose 3 maps from n
        long totalWays = comb(n, 3);
        
        // Count favorable cases
        long favorable = 0;
        
        // Case 1: All 3 selected maps are studied
        if (studied >= 3) {
            favorable += comb(studied, 3);
        }
        
        // Case 2: Exactly 2 studied maps and 1 non-studied map
        if (studied >= 2 && n - studied >= 1) {
            // When 2 studied and 1 non-studied are shown:
            // Johnny will pick one of the 2 studied maps to discard
            // Opponent picks randomly among 3 maps
            // Game will be played on the remaining studied map if:
            // - Opponent discards the non-studied map AND Johnny discards one studied map
            // - Or opponent discards one studied map AND Johnny discards the other studied map
            
            // Total ways opponent can pick: 3 choices
            // Johnny will always pick one of the studied maps to discard
            
            // If opponent picks non-studied: probability = 1/3, then game goes to one of 2 studied maps (both studied)
            // If opponent picks studied: probability = 2/3, then game goes to either the other studied or non-studied
            
            // Actually, let's recalculate more carefully:
            // When 2 studied (S1, S2) and 1 non-studied (N) are shown:
            // Johnny will discard one studied map (say S1)
            // Opponent discards randomly among 3
            
            // If opponent discards S1: game goes to random of {S2, N} -> 1/2 chance studied
            // If opponent discards S2: game goes to random of {S1, N} -> 1/2 chance studied  
            // If opponent discards N: game goes to random of {S1, S2} -> 1 chance studied
            
            // Since Johnny discards randomly among his 2 studied maps, and opponent discards randomly:
            // Probability = (1/3)*(1/2) + (1/3)*(1/2) + (1/3)*1 = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/3 = 2/3
            
            favorable += comb(studied, 2) * (n - studied) * 2; // 2/3 probability, but we need to account for this
        }
        
        // Case 3: Exactly 1 studied map and 2 non-studied maps
        if (studied >= 1 && n - studied >= 2) {
            // When 1 studied (S) and 2 non-studied (N1, N2) are shown:
            // Johnny will discard the non-studied map (one of 2 choices)
            // Opponent discards randomly among 3
            
            // If opponent discards S: game goes to random of {N1, N2} -> 0 chance studied
            // If opponent discards N1: game goes to random of {S, N2} -> 1/2 chance studied
            // If opponent discards N2: game goes to random of {S, N1} -> 1/2 chance studied
            
            // Johnny discards one of the 2 non-studied maps randomly
            // Probability = (1/3)*0 + (1/3)*(1/2) + (1/3)*(1/2) = 1/3
            
            favorable += studied * comb(n - studied, 2) * 1; // 1/3 probability
        }
        
        // Case 4: 0 studied maps - already handled by studied==0 case
        
        // But the above approach is getting complex. Let's use a cleaner approach:
        // For each combination of 3 maps, calculate the probability that the final map is studied
        
        return calculateProbabilityDetailed(n, studied);
    }
    
    public static double calculateProbabilityDetailed(int n, int studied) {
        if (studied == 0) return 0.0;
        if (n < 3) return 0.0;
        
        double totalProb = 0.0;
        int totalCombinations = comb(n, 3);
        
        // Iterate through all possible combinations of 3 maps
        // We'll count based on how many studied maps are in the 3 selected
        
        for (int studiedInThree = 0; studiedInThree <= Math.min(3, studied); studiedInThree++) {
            if (studiedInThree > studied || (3 - studiedInThree) > (n - studied)) continue;
            
            int nonStudiedInThree = 3 - studiedInThree;
            long combinations = (long)comb(studied, studiedInThree) * comb(n - studied, nonStudiedInThree);
            
            if (combinations == 0) continue;
            
            double probGivenThisConfig = 0.0;
            
            if (studiedInThree == 0) {
                probGivenThisConfig = 0.0;
            } else if (studiedInThree == 1) {
                // 1 studied, 2 non-studied
                // Johnny discards one non-studied (2 choices)
                // Opponent discards randomly among 3
                // If opponent discards studied (1/3): game goes to random of 2 non-studied -> 0
                // If opponent discards non-studied (2/3): game goes to random of {studied, other non-studied} -> 1/2
                // But Johnny chooses which non-studied to discard, so:
                // If Johnny discards N1: opponent discards S -> {N2}, opponent discards N2 -> {S, N1}, opponent discards N1 -> {S, N2}
                // Actually, Johnny will always discard a non-studied map
                // So: opponent discards studied (1/3): final map is random of 2 non-studied -> 0
                //     opponent discards N1 (1/3): final map is random of {S, N2} -> 1/2
                //     opponent discards N2 (1/3): final map is random of {S, N1} -> 1/2
                // Since Johnny picks randomly which non-studied to discard, and both non-studied are symmetric:
                // Probability = (1/3)*0 + (1/3)*(1/2) + (1/3)*(1/2) = 1/3
                probGivenThisConfig = 1.0 / 3.0;
            } else if (studiedInThree == 2) {
                // 2 studied, 1 non-studied
                // Johnny discards one studied (2 choices)
                // Opponent discards randomly among 3
                // If opponent discards studied1 (1/3): final map is random of {studied2, non-studied} -> 1/2
                // If opponent discards studied2 (1/3): final map is random of {studied1, non-studied} -> 1/2
                // If opponent discards non-studied (1/3): final map is random of {studied1, studied2} -> 1
                // Since Johnny picks randomly which studied to discard, and both studied are symmetric:
                // Probability = (1/3)*(1/2) + (1/3)*(1/2) + (1/3)*1 = 2/3
                probGivenThisConfig = 2.0 / 3.0;
            } else if (studiedInThree == 3) {
                // 3 studied
                // Johnny discards one studied (3 choices)
                // Opponent discards randomly among 3
                // No matter what, the final map will be studied
                probGivenThisConfig = 1.0;
            }
            
            totalProb += (double)combinations * probGivenThisConfig;
        }
        
        return totalProb / totalCombinations;
    }
    
    // Calculate combination C(n, k)
    public static int comb(int n, int k) {
        if (k > n || k < 0) return 0;
        if (k == 0 || k == n) return 1;
        
        long result = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
            result = result * (n - i + 1) / i;
        }
        return (int)result;
    }
}
